thread:
maya: Heads-up - ran a FP8 vs GPTQ vs INT8 sweep on the summarization eval set with prefix cache enabled. Strange accuracy shift when continuous batching is on.
jon: ugh, details? numbers? dataset?
maya: eval set = internal-news-10k, ROUGE-L / EM. Baseline FP16 = ROUGE-L 42.1, EM 27.5.
maya: FP8 (quant-params=v1) + prefix cache on + continuous batch = ROUGE-L 40.2, EM 25.9 -> ~2 pts drop.
maya: GPTQ-int8 (per-channel) + same cache/batch = ROUGE-L 41.8, EM 27.1.
ashley: so FP8 is worse only when both prefix cache & continuous batching are enabled?
maya: yes. FP8 w/o cache but with batching = 41.9. FP8 w/ cache but batching disabled = 41.7.
kevin: suggests an interaction: FP8's kv-cache representation + our continuous batching fusion might be clobbering keys. Could be rounding + stale cache.
jon: any logs or assertion failures?
maya: no crash. Latency improved: p95 token latency down 12% for FP8+batching. But output quality drops.
kevin: can you paste the config we used?
maya: sure:

```
model: my-s2s-xl
quant: fp8-dp8
kv_cache: prefix_cache_enabled: true
batching: continuous: true
batch_window_ms: 6
```

kevin: hmmm, batch_window_ms=6 is aggressive. Could cause requests to share a KV state incorrectly if serialization isn't guarded.
ashley: we saw a similar off-by-one in the cache pointer when memory is quantized for AWQ earlier. Might be index truncation.
maya: ran a short repro: turned on extra cache validation metric that checks KV checksum per request. FP8 shows checksum drift after 3-4 tokens when continuous batching merges strides. GPTQ-int8 no drift.
jon: can you push the repro and CI job? add CI job to run on smaller model and synthetic workload.
maya: pushed branch and CI job: ci-bot: build/quant-batch-repro #182 started.
ci-bot: build/quant-batch-repro #182 succeeded in 18m.
maya: attached minimal log snippet:

```
[req=abc123] step=gen token=3 kv_checksum=0x7a1b
[req=def456] step=3 kv_checksum=0x7a1b
[req=abc123] step=4 kv_checksum=0x6f2c  <-- drift
```

kevin: that drift aligns with small-rounding in FP8 accumulation. I think the batching fusion re-uses a temporary buffer without re-quantizing per-request.
ashley: quick experiment: try FP8 + force-per-request-quantization (disable buffer reuse) and see accuracy.
maya: did that. FP8 + per-request quantize + prefix cache + continuous batch -> ROUGE-L 41.8, EM 27.0 (nearly recovered). Latency lost ~4% vs aggressive FP8.
jon: tradeoff looks acceptable if we can gate per-request quantize behind a config flag per-customer. For Dedicated customers who want max perf, maybe offer opt-in.
kevin: longer term fix: enforce checksum invariants in runtime and adjust fusion to not share quant state across requests. Also add fuzz tests for quantized kv-copies.
ashley: agree. Add an eval to Redwood Optimize that flags >1pt drop when using quant+cache+batching combos.
maya: I'll open PR with fixes and rollout plan. Plan: 1) feature-flag per-request-quantize default ON for FP8 with prefix cache, 2) add regression alerts, 3) performance tuning to recover the 4% latency.
jon: timeline?
maya: PR today, CI passes, can canary to staging tomorrow, monitor ROUGE/EM and p95 for 48h.
ops-bot: deploy to staging scheduled: canary/quant-fp8-cache @ 2025-03-05T09:00Z
kevin: thanks. one more ask - add the small synthetic test to nightly so we catch regressions early.
maya: added to nightly. will follow up with PR link after merge. :thumbsup:
